attack_scenario: should_strip_auth() also drops the header when scheme or port change, except an http->https upgrade on default ports
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix

attack_scenario: A client sends Authorization to https://api.example.com, which redirects to http://api.example.com; the same hostname keeps the header, so the credentials go out over plain HTTP
remediation: Strip Authorization when the scheme or port changes on redirect, not only the hostname (allowing only http->https on default ports)
source: Requests (Apache-2.0, Copyright 2019 Kenneth Reitz), requests/sessions.py

attack_scenario: Matches are re-checked with a Unicode-aware comparison and the mail goes to the address stored on the account
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/contrib/auth/forms.py

attack_scenario: Attacker requests a reset for an address that matches the victim's only under Unicode case folding (e.g., a dotless i); the reset link is mailed to the attacker's address
remediation: Compare emails with NFKC normalisation and casefold, and send the mail to the address stored on the user, not the one typed in the form
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/contrib/auth/forms.py

attack_scenario: putrequest() rejects any method with characters outside the HTTP token set, so CR and LF cannot reach the request line
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: urllib3 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2008-2020 Andrey Petrov and contributors), src/urllib3/connection.py

attack_scenario: An app lets the user choose the HTTP method; a method like 'GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nX-Injected: 1\r\n' adds headers or a second request (CRLF injection)
remediation: Reject methods containing anything other than HTTP token characters before calling putrequest
source: urllib3 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2008-2020 Andrey Petrov and contributors), src/urllib3/connection.py

attack_scenario: The delimiter is wrapped in Value() and sent as a bound parameter, so it cannot change the SQL
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/contrib/postgres/aggregates/general.py and mixins.py

attack_scenario: An app passes a user-chosen delimiter to StringAgg; delimiter="') FROM x; DROP TABLE y; --" breaks out of the quoted literal in the SQL template
remediation: Pass the delimiter as a query parameter (Value(str(delimiter))) instead of formatting it into the SQL template
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/contrib/postgres/aggregates/general.py and mixins.py

attack_scenario: safe_join() raises when the joined path leaves the template directory
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/contrib/admindocs/views.py

attack_scenario: A staff user requests the admindocs template page with template=../../../../etc/passwd and the file content is shown
remediation: Build the path with django.utils._os.safe_join(directory, template), which refuses paths outside the directory
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/contrib/admindocs/views.py

attack_scenario: Endpoint patterns end with \Z and are matched with fullmatch, so a trailing newline no longer matches
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/urls/resolvers.py

attack_scenario: A proxy blocks /admin/ by path, but Django's $-terminated patterns also match a path with a trailing newline (/admin%0A), so the request reaches the protected view
remediation: Use fullmatch (or \Z instead of $) for endpoint patterns so a trailing newline does not match
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/urls/resolvers.py

attack_scenario: check_alias() rejects any alias containing quotes, whitespace, semicolons, or comment markers
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/db/models/sql/query.py

attack_scenario: An app passes user-controlled keys as **kwargs to annotate() or extra(select=...); a key like 'x" FROM t; --' becomes a raw column alias in the SQL
remediation: Reject aliases containing quotes, whitespace, semicolons, or SQL comments before using them
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/db/models/sql/query.py

attack_scenario: prepare_key() refuses every PEM block and every SSH key format, so a public key cannot be used as an HMAC secret
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: PyJWT (MIT, Copyright (c) 2015-2022 Jose Padilla), jwt/algorithms.py and jwt/utils.py

attack_scenario: A verifier that accepts several algorithms is given its Ed25519 or ECDSA public key; the attacker signs a token with HS256 using that public key as the HMAC secret and it verifies
remediation: Refuse any key that looks like a PEM or SSH public key in HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key, for all PEM and SSH formats
source: PyJWT (MIT, Copyright (c) 2015-2022 Jose Padilla), jwt/algorithms.py and jwt/utils.py

attack_scenario: as_sql() rejects any lookup_name that does not fully match a strict word pattern before it reaches the SQL
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/db/models/functions/datetime.py and django/db/backends/postgresql/operations.py

attack_scenario: An app builds Extract(field, lookup_name=request.GET['part']); a crafted lookup_name is formatted into EXTRACT('%s' FROM ...) unescaped
remediation: Validate lookup_name against a strict pattern (letters, digits, -, _, parentheses) before building the SQL
source: Django (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) Django Software Foundation and individual contributors), django/db/models/functions/datetime.py and django/db/backends/postgresql/operations.py

attack_scenario: Proxy-Authorization is only re-added when the scheme is not https, so it never enters the TLS tunnel
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix
source: Requests (Apache-2.0, Copyright 2019 Kenneth Reitz), requests/sessions.py

attack_scenario: A client uses an authenticated proxy for HTTPS; on a redirect, Proxy-Authorization is re-added to the tunneled request and the destination server receives the proxy credentials
remediation: Only add Proxy-Authorization for non-HTTPS schemes; urllib3 handles proxy auth for tunneled requests
source: Requests (Apache-2.0, Copyright 2019 Kenneth Reitz), requests/sessions.py

attack_scenario: Keys containing whitespace raise ValueError, so a key cannot inject an extra attribute
remediation: None needed; this is the code after the upstream fix

remediation: Reject attribute keys that contain whitespace before building the attribute string
source: Jinja (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright 2007 Pallets), src/jinja2/filters.py

attack_scenario: safe_join() also rejects names starting with '/', which covers UNC paths that ntpath.isabs misses

attack_scenario: Attacker sets the cart cookie to a crafted pickle whose __reduce__ runs os.system, getting code execution on the server
remediation: Store the cart as JSON and parse it with json.loads, or sign the cookie and never unpickle client data
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-502 page and the project brief key example

attack_scenario: Attacker requests name=../config/secrets.env and reads files outside the reports folder
remediation: Resolve the path with os.path.realpath and reject it unless it stays inside REPORT_DIR
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-22 page and the project brief key example

attack_scenario: An anonymous user sends DELETE /admin/users/u2 and removes an account without logging in
remediation: Protect the route with the same @login_required decorator and an admin role check
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-862 page

attack_scenario: Logged-in user ana requests /invoices/102 and reads raj's invoice by changing the id
remediation: Return 404 unless invoice['owner'] equals the logged-in user
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-639 page

attack_scenario: Attacker asks for url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ and the server fetches cloud credentials from the internal metadata service
remediation: Allow only https URLs whose resolved host is on an allowlist and not a private or link-local address
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-918 page

attack_scenario: The app listens on 0.0.0.0 with the Werkzeug debugger on; anyone who triggers an error gets an interactive Python console
remediation: Never pass debug=True in deployed code; read it from config that defaults to off and bind to 127.0.0.1 in development
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-489 page

attack_scenario: Attacker posts an order whose DTD defines an entity pointing to file:///etc/passwd; the file content comes back in the customer field
remediation: Parse with defusedxml, or create the lxml parser with resolve_entities=False and load_dtd=False
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-611 page

attack_scenario: After a database leak, unsalted MD5 hashes are cracked in seconds with rainbow tables or a GPU
remediation: Hash passwords with a slow salted KDF, e.g., werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash or bcrypt/argon2
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-328 page

attack_scenario: Anyone who reads the source signs their own session cookie with the known key and becomes any user
remediation: Load SECRET_KEY from an environment variable or secret manager and rotate it
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-321 page

attack_scenario: random uses a Mersenne Twister; an attacker who collects enough outputs predicts the next reset token and takes over the account
remediation: Generate tokens with secrets.token_urlsafe() or secrets.choice()
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-338 page

attack_scenario: Attacker sends host=127.0.0.1;cat /etc/passwd and the shell runs the second command
remediation: Validate the host with ipaddress.ip_address and call subprocess.run with an argument list and no shell
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-78 page

attack_scenario: Attacker sends formula=__import__('os').system('id') and the server runs it
remediation: Parse the formula with a small expression parser (e.g., ast with an allowlist of nodes) instead of eval
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-95 page

attack_scenario: Attacker sends to={{ config.items() }} (or a payload reaching os.popen) and Jinja2 evaluates it on the server
remediation: Keep the template constant and pass the recipient as a variable: render_template_string('... {{ recipient }} ...', recipient=recipient)
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-1336 page

attack_scenario: Anyone with read access to the repo logs into the ops console with the password in the source
remediation: Read the admin credential hash from a secret store or environment and compare with check_password_hash
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-798 page

attack_scenario: Anyone who reads the users table (backup, SQL error, insider) gets every password in clear text and reuses them elsewhere
remediation: Store generate_password_hash(password) and verify with check_password_hash
source: Written by us, based on the CWE-256 page
